rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation from earth is general creation as previously explained; alternatively, humans derive from semen formed from foods whose origin is earth.
rows.anchor: إنشاءا إجماليا حسبما مر بحقيقه وقيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, humans are from earth because semen derives from foods originating in the earth.
rows.anchor: المني الذي يتكونون منه من الأغذية التي منشؤها من الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first إذ is a temporal adverb modifying أعلم and retains its ordinary comparative sense.
rows.anchor: فإذا ظرف لأعلم وهو على بابه من التفضيل

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: Makki takes إذ to mean that God is the sole knower of their circumstances then; al-Alusi objects that God could inform angels of them.
rows.anchor: وقال مكي : هو بمعنى عالم غذ تعلق علمه تعالى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another proposal makes إذ governed by an omitted imperative, ‘remember when He created you’; al-Alusi dismisses it.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ( إذ ) منصوب بمحذوف والتقدير اذكروا

words: وَإِذْ أَنتُمْ أَجِنَّةٌۭ فِى بُطُونِ أُمَّهَٰتِكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Embryos develop through ordered stages, all their states and deeds—including lapses—known to God; without His vast forgiveness, consequences would strike them.
rows.anchor: على أطوار مختلفة مترتبة لا يخفى عليه سبحانه حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning the mothers’ wombs, though embryos are necessarily inside them, points to their successive stages.
rows.anchor: وذكر ( فيبطون أمهاتكم ) مع أن الجنين ما كان

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the womb phrase underscores God's knowledge because the womb is intensely dark.
rows.anchor: وقيل : لتأكيد شأن العلم لما أن بطن الأم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The فاء connects the ban to the preceding point: lapses go unpunished through divine forgiveness, not because they are not sins.
rows.anchor: والفاء في قوله تعالى : ( فلا تزكوا أنفسكم ( لترتيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not claim complete freedom from sin or purity and superiority in good works; acknowledge God's favor and forgiveness.
rows.anchor: فلا تثنوا على أنفسكم بالطهارة عن المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This resumption reinforces the ban on self-praise and indicates that some people avoid every sin.
rows.anchor: فيهم من يتقيهابأسرها كذافي الإرشاد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other interpretations take piety as avoiding shirk, or avoiding some sins.
rows.anchor: وقيل : اتقى الشرك وقيل : اتقى شيئا من المعاصي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The verse was reportedly revealed about believers listing their prayers, fasting, and pilgrimage; this is blameworthy when done from vanity or ostentation, but otherwise permissible.
rows.anchor: والآية نزلت على ما قيل : في قوم من المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking pleasure in obedience is itself obedience, and mentioning it can be gratitude.
rows.anchor: ولذا قيل : المسرة بالطاعة طاعة وذكرها شكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Self-purification can be conveyed by gestures as well as words, including names implying purity.
rows.anchor: ولا فرق في التزكية بين أن تكون عبارة وأن تكون إشارة

rows.speaker: زينب بنت أبي سلمة
rows.claim: When Zaynab bint Abi Salama was named Barra, the Prophet said God knows the truly pious and renamed her Zaynab; Ahmad, Muslim, Abu Dawud, Ibn Mardawayh, and Ibn Saʿd transmit it.
rows.anchor: عن زينب بنت أبي سلمة أنها سميت برة فقال رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet also changed Barra bint Jahsh’s name; changing such names is recommended.
rows.anchor: غير عليه الصلاة والسلام إلى ذلك اسم برة بنت جحش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Names such as Baraka and Yasar, which may invite ill omen, are discouraged for tanzih; al-Nawawi reads the reported ban on Nafiʿ, Aflah, and Baraka as prohibitive.
rows.anchor: كما روي جابر : إن عشت إن الله أنهى أمتي أن يسموا نافعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dislike applies where a name’s implication of praise is strong and conventionally explicit; names like Saʿid and Hasan are not objectionable.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن كراهة ما يشعر بالتزكية مخصوص بما إذاكان الإشعار قويا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Umar reportedly renamed a daughter called ʿAsiya as Jamila, though al-Alusi notes that the discussion merits further review.
rows.anchor: ابنة يقال لها : عاصية فسماها رصص جميلة كذا قيل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reading forbids people to praise one another for reputation or worldly gain or to certify virtue absolutely; testimony establishing rights remains allowed.
rows.anchor: وقيل : معنى لا تزكوا أنفسكم لا يزكي بعضكم بعضا

rows.speaker: ثابت بن الحارث الأنصاري
rows.claim: Thabit reports that Jews called a deceased infant a ṣiddiq; the Prophet rejected this, saying God knows every fetus’s felicity or misery, and this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن ثابت بن الحرث الأنصاري قال كانت اليهود إذاهلك لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s reference is to what was in his revealed scrolls; he fulfilled what he was commanded or completely honored his covenant with God.
rows.anchor: وبما في صحف إبراهيم التي نزلت عليه ( الذي وفى ( أي وفر وأتم ما أمر به

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Abraham fulfilled all ten ‘shares of Islam,’ which no one else did: ten in 9:111, ten in 33:35, six at the start of 23:1, and four in 70:26.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : وفى بسهام الإسلام كلها ولم يوفها

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة
rows.claim: A weak raised report from Abu Umama says Abraham fulfilled four rakʿas that he prayed each day, in one version at the day’s beginning.
rows.anchor: عن أبي أمامة يرفعه وفى بأربع ركعات يصليهن في كل يوم

rows.speaker: معاذ بن أنس
rows.claim: A raised report from Muʿadh ibn Anas says God called Abraham His intimate because he fulfilled; he recited the morning-and-evening glorification in 30:17.
rows.anchor: وأخرج أحمد من حديث معاذبن أنس مرفوعا أيضا ألا أخبركم

rows.speaker: معاذ بن أنس
rows.claim: The report gives Abraham’s repeated morning and evening glorification as the practice in view.
rows.anchor: كلما أصبح وأمسى سبحان الله حين تمسو وحين تصبحون الآية

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima explains fulfillment as conveying the ten obligations beginning ‘no bearer bears another’s burden.’
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة : ( وفي ) بتبليغ هذه العشرة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reports the general interpretation, which al-Alusi prefers: Abraham fulfilled every command God gave him.
rows.anchor: والأولى العموم وهو مروي عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham was singled out for this quality because of what he endured; the sacrifice story alone suffices as evidence.
rows.anchor: وتخصيصه عليه السلام بهذا الوصف لاحتمالأما لايحتمله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation for naming these prophets is that earlier peoples assigned a person relatives’ sins; Abraham first opposed this, and Moses confirmed the rule.
rows.anchor: قيل : لأنه فيما بين نوح وإبراهيم كانوا يأخذون الرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham is mentioned first because his scrolls were better known and more familiar to the audience.
rows.anchor: وتقديمه لماصحفه أشهر عندهم وأكثر

rows.speaker: أبو أمامة الباهلي وسعيد بن جبير وأبو مالك الغفاري وابن السمقيع وزيد بن علي
rows.claim: These readers pronounce the fāʾ lightly in وَفَى.
rows.anchor: وقرأأبو أمامة الباهلي وسعيد بن جبير وأبو مالك الغفاري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أن is a lightened form of heavy أنَّ with an omitted subject pronoun referring to the matter; the negative clause is its predicate and replaces material in Moses’ scrolls or predicates an omitted subject.
rows.anchor: على أن ( أن ) هي المخففة من الثقيلة وضمير الشأن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No person is punished for another’s sin so that the other can escape punishment.
rows.anchor: لا يؤاخذ أحد بذنب غيره ليتخلص الثاني عن عقابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s warning that an originator of an evil practice bears its burden and followers’ burdens is no contradiction: misleading others is the originator’s own sin.
rows.anchor: من سن سنة سيئة فعليه وزرها ووزر من عمل بها إلى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person receives recompense for his effort; Arabic can say God recompensed him by his work, for his work, or directly with the work by omitting the preposition.
rows.anchor: أي يجزى الإنسان سعيه يقالأ : جزاه الله عز وجل بعمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الجزاء الأوفى may be a verbal noun specifying the kind of recompense; describing the recompense as most complete licenses describing its event likewise by association.
rows.anchor: مصدر مبين للنوع وإذا جاز وصف المجزي به بالأوفى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, الجزاء is the thing recompensed, effectively giving the verb three objects; some instead analyze it as an object after omission of a preposition.
rows.anchor: وجوز كونه مفعولا بهبمعنى المجزيبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another analysis makes the pronoun refer to recompense rather than effort, with الجزاء الأوفى as apposition or explanatory substitute.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون الضمير المنصوب في ( يجزاه ) للجزاء لا للسعي

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan objects that the analysis substitutes an explicit noun for a pronoun; al-Alusi says the correct position forbids this disputed construction.
rows.anchor: وتعقبه أبو حيان أن فيهإبدال الظاهر من الضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone causes death and life; the emphatic pronoun and repeated attribution establish exclusive agency.
rows.anchor: وتقديم الضمير وتكرير الإسناد للحصر أي أنه تعالى فعل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ordinary sense of making people laugh and weep also fits death and life: death commonly brings tears, while birth brings laughter.
rows.anchor: والموت يعقبه البكاء غالبا والإحياء عند الولاد الضحك

rows.speaker: مجاهد والكلبي
rows.claim: Mujahid and al-Kalbi interpret God’s making laugh and weep as making the people of Paradise laugh and the people of Hell weep.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد والكلبي : ( أضحك ) أهل الجنة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation says God makes the earth laugh with vegetation and the sky weep with rain.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ( أضحك ) الأرض بالنبات ( وأبكى ) السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one besides God causes death or life: a killer only dismantles the human body, while God brings about death through His customary order.
rows.anchor: فلا يقدر على الإماتة والإحياء غير عز وجل والقاتل إنماينقض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The quoted poet contrasts a baby born crying among joyful onlookers with a person dying amid mourners who rejoice.
rows.anchor: ولدتك أمك يا ابن آدم باكيا والناس حولك يضحكون سرورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other origination is resurrection after death, fulfilling God’s promise.
rows.anchor: أي الأحياء بعدالإماتة وفاءابوعده جل شأنه

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Al-Baḥr says the emphasis on ‘upon Him’ addresses deniers, making resurrection sound imposed by God upon Himself.
rows.anchor: لما كانت هذه النشأة ينكرها الكفار بولغ بقوله تعالى عليه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says resurrection is required by wisdom so God can reward good and evil; al-Alusi questions this Muʿtazilite approach.
rows.anchor: وفي الكشاف قال سبحانه : ( عليه ) لأنها واجبة في الحكمة

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu ʿAmr lengthen the hamza in النشأة; this remains a verbal noun of Form I نشأ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو النشأة بالمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing oath after each of four stories confirms the preceding warning that reports had come to them; each story alone warranted reflection and deterrence, yet they did not learn.
rows.anchor: جملة قسمية وردت في آخر القصص الأربع تقريرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the Quran accessible by revealing it in the audience’s language, filling it with exhortation and examples, and alternating warning with promise.
rows.anchor: سهلنا القرآن لقومك بأن أنزلناه على لغتهم وشحناه بأنواع المواعظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here dhikr means taking heed and receiving admonition.
rows.anchor: أي للتذكر والأتعاظ فهل من مدكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question emphatically denies the existence of anyone who takes heed: no respondent could answer yes.
rows.anchor: فهل من مدكر إنكار ونفي للمتعظ على أبلغ وجه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes ‘made easy’ to mean easy to memorize, owing to its fine structure, eloquent wording, noble true meanings, and lack of obscure expressions.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المعنى سهلنا القرآن للحفظ لما اشتمل عليه من حسن النظم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: On the memorization reading, the question asks whether anyone seeks to memorize it so divine aid may support him.
rows.anchor: فهل من طالب لحفظه ليعان عليه

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr says no divine scripture besides the Quran has been memorized.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جبير : لم يستظهر شيء من الكتب الإلهية

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses the verse as God having made Quran recitation easy.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد أنه قال : يسرنا القرآن هونا قراءته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says that without God’s making it easy on human tongues, no creature could speak God’s speech.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس لو لا أن الله تعالى يسره على لسان الآدميين

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Al-Daylami transmits a raised report from Anas making the same point about God enabling people to speak the Quran.
rows.anchor: وأخرج الديلمي عن أنس مرفوعا

rows.speaker: ابن سيرين
rows.claim: Ibn Sirin corrected someone who called a sura ‘light’: say ‘easy,’ following God’s description of the Quran.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذرعن ابن سيرين أنه مر برجل يقول سورة خفيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The admonition reading best fits the context; if authentic, the Anas report need not be an explanation of this verse.
rows.anchor: والمعنى الذي ذكر أولاأنسب بالمقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yassarnā may mean ‘prepared,’ as when one saddles a camel for travel or a horse for battle; the cited poetry witnesses this usage.
rows.anchor: وجوز ( يسرنا ) بهيأنا منقولهم : يسر ناقته للسفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created every created thing by measure, written in the Preserved Tablet before occurring; qadar here has its familiar sense contrasted with qaḍāʾ.
rows.anchor: مكتوبا في اللوحقبلوقوعه فالقدر بالمعنى المشهور

rows.speaker: كثير من السلف
rows.claim: This interpretation of qadar as predestination is transmitted from many early authorities.
rows.anchor: هو المأثور عن كثير من السلف

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that Quraysh polytheists disputed predestination with the Prophet, whereupon the verses about being dragged into Hell and creation by measure were revealed; Ahmad, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Majah transmit it.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : جاء مشركو قريش يخاصمون رسول الله

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas transmits the Prophet’s statement that the Murjiʾa and Qadariyya have no share in Islam and that verses beginning ‘the sinners are in error and fire’ concern them; al-Tirmidhi grades it ḥasan.
rows.anchor: عنابن عباس قال : قال رسول الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas strongly disliked the Qadariyya; Abu Yahya al-Aʿraj heard him threaten them and say adultery, theft, and drinking wine occur by decree.
rows.anchor: عن أبي يحيى الأعرج قال سمعتابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Mujahid asked Ibn Abbas what he would do to someone denying predestination; Ibn Abbas said to bring the person so he could choke him to death.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد أنه قال : قلتلابن عباس : ما تقول فيمن يكذب بالقدر

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet calls deniers of decree the Magians of his community and says not to visit them when ill or attend their funerals; Ahmad, Abu Dawud, and al-Tabarani transmit from Ibn Umar.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمران أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : لكل أمة مجوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, creation by measure means each thing was precisely fashioned in accord with the wisdom governing creation, as in 25:2.
rows.anchor: وجوز كون المعنى إنا كل شي خلقناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the transmitted accusative, كل is governed by a verb understood from the following verb: ‘We created every thing.’
rows.anchor: ونصب ( كل ) بفعل يفسره ما بعدهأي إنا خلقنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse establishes that everything created is measured; ‘every thing’ means every created thing, not all infinitely many possibles, which God did not create.
rows.anchor: على أن كل شيء مخلوق بقدر ولا ينبغي أن تجعل

rows.speaker: أبو السمال وابن عطية وقوم من أهل السنة
rows.claim: Abu al-Sammal, as Ibn Atiyya notes, and a group of Sunnis read كل in the nominative; it is then a subject, with خلقناه as predicate.
rows.anchor: وقرا أبو السمال قال : ابن عطية وقوممن أهل السنة

rows.speaker: الرضي
rows.claim: Al-Raḍi says the readings need not differ: كل refers to created things in either parse, so every thing God created is measured.
rows.anchor: وقال الرضي : لا يتفاوتالمعنى لأن مراده تعالى بكل شيء كل مخلوق

rows.speaker: الرضي
rows.claim: Al-Raḍi distinguishes the predicate parse (‘every thing We created is measured’) from the adjectival parse (‘every thing created by Us is measured’), but sees both as restricted to created things.
rows.anchor: خلقناه هو الخبر ( كل ) مخلوق مخلوق ( بقدر )

rows.speaker: السيد السند
rows.claim: Al-Sayyid al-Sanad objects that the adjectival parse leaves room for other created things outside the ruling, unlike predicate or accusative parses; the sentence does not communicate that they share the attribute.
rows.anchor: وتعقبه السيد السند قدس سره

rows.speaker: الشهاب الخفاجي
rows.claim: Al-Shihab al-Khafaji makes a similar objection; al-Alusi concludes that the accusative reading states the intended meaning most explicitly and outweighs a potentially misleading nominative parse despite requiring ellipsis.
rows.anchor: وذكر نحوه الشهاب الخفاجي ولكونالنصب نصافي المقصود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘All upon it’ means those on the earth prepared for living beings, including animals and composite bodies.
rows.anchor: على الأرض التي وضعت للأنام من الحيوانات والمركبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative pronoun من either includes things with rational beings predominant or specifically denotes humans and jinn.
rows.anchor: و ( من ) للتغليب أو للثقلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi interprets God’s face as His essence, with a descriptive attribution; using a bodily face for essence is a common metonym, like ‘hands’ for persons.
rows.anchor: أي ذاته عز وجل والمراد هو سبحانه وتعالى فالإضافة بيانية

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says face originally means direction and its use for essence is allusive; al-Alusi identifies the essence interpretation with later theologians’ taʾwil, unlike the Salaf’s method.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أصله الجهة واستعماله في الذاتمن باب الكناية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address apparently honors the Prophet; another view addresses anyone suited to receive the grave message.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الخطاب في ربك للرسول صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some take face as intention, meaning deeds intended for God; al-Alusi finds this problematic.
rows.anchor: ما قيل : الوجه بمعنى القصد ويراد به المقصود

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A closer alternative takes face as the direction God commanded people to face and approach: righteous deeds remain for reward, but this does not fit the context of universal perishing.
rows.anchor: وأقرب منه ما قيل : وجهه تعالى الجهة التي أمرنا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view makes the face the divine direction God attends to and bestows; that aspect remains while each thing itself perishes continually.
rows.anchor: وقيل : وجهه سبحانه الجهة التي يليها الحق أي يتولاها بفضله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A metaphysical reading takes God’s face as a possible being’s relation to Him; considered independent of the true existent that causes it, the possible is nonexistent.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المراد بوجهه سبحانه وجهه الممكن وهي جهة حيثية ارتباطه

rows.speaker: البيضاوي
rows.claim: Al-Bayḍawi says all aspects of beings perish in themselves except the aspect turned toward God; scholars differ whether this continues his earlier essence interpretation or adds another.
rows.anchor: وقول العلامة البيضاوي : لو استقرت جهات الموجودات وتفحصت وجوهها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi distinguishes actual existence inhering in possibles (most philosophers and theologians) from metaphorical existence; the latter divides into the ‘theistic’ philosophers’ manifestation model and realized Sufis’ one-essence model.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنها إما موجودة حقيقة بمعنى أنها متصفة بالوجود

rows.speaker: المتألهون من الحكماء
rows.claim: For the ‘theistic’ philosophers, possibles are mirrors manifesting self-subsistent divine existence; their differing relation to the Necessary gives distinct reflections, and paths to God equal creatures’ breaths.
rows.anchor: وإليه ذهب المتأهلون من الحكماء والمحققون من الصوفية

rows.speaker: المحققون من الصوفية
rows.claim: Realized Sufis posit one essence with multiple attributes, aspects, and renewed manifestations, rather than multiple necessary and possible essences; the two mystical accounts are commonly treated alike.
rows.anchor: ومذاق المحققين من الصوفية أن علاقة المجاز أنها بمنزلة صفات قائمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the real-existence view, face is existence bestowed on possibles by the Necessary through ‘necessity by another,’ the honored aspect nearest intrinsic necessity.
rows.anchor: ووجه التطبيق على الول أن يقال : المراد من الوجه الذي يلي جهته تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the philosophers’ metaphorical account, face is the special relation to the divine presence that permits calling a possible existent, as God’s manifestation.
rows.anchor: ووجه التطبيقعلى الثاني أن يقال : الوجه الذي يلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the realized Sufi account, created things are nonexistent in every respect except as divine affairs and considerations.
rows.anchor: ووجه التطبيق على الثالث أن يقالأ : المراد بالوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can describe the awe monotheists feel before God, His intrinsic perfection beyond comprehension, or His majesty and generosity toward them.
rows.anchor: أي يجله الموحدون عن التشبيه بخلقه ويثبتون له ما يليق بشأنه

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: Some scholars gloss majesty as absolute independence and generosity as complete favor; majesty entails transcendence and needlessness, as al-Jawhari notes.
rows.anchor: وفسر بعض المحققين ( الجلال ) بالأستغناء المطلق

rows.speaker: الكرماني
rows.claim: Al-Kirmani classifies negative attributes such as having no partner as majesty and positive attributes such as life and knowledge as generosity; al-Alusi says this needs examination.
rows.anchor: وقال الكرماني : إنه تعالى لهصفات عدمية مثل ( لا شريك له )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ذو apparently modifies face: creation’s extinction cannot impair God’s self-sufficiency, and He will bestow generosity on humans and jinn after they perish.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن ( ذو ) صفة للوجه ويتضمن الوصف بما ذكر

rows.speaker: أبي وعبد الله
rows.claim: If face means righteous action or direction, some parse ذو as a detached predicate referring to the Lord; the genitive reading ذي by Ubayy and Ibn Masʿud supports attachment to Lord.
rows.anchor: ويؤيده قراءة أبي وعبد الله ذيالجلال بالياء

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says this title belongs uniquely to God and is among His greatest descriptions.
rows.anchor: وذكر الراغب أن هذا الوصف قد خص به عز وجل

rows.speaker: أنس وربيعة بن عامر
rows.claim: Raised reports from Anas and Rabiʿa ibn ʿAmir urge frequent invocation of this name; al-Alusi explains ألظوا as adhering to and repeating it in supplication.
rows.anchor: ما رواه الترمذي عن أنس والإمام أحمد عن ربيعة بن عامر

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reports a man’s supplication using this name; the Prophet says he invoked God by His greatest name, by which He answers and grants requests.
rows.anchor: وروي الترمذي وأبو داود والنسائي عن أنس أنه كان مع رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction introduces two further gardens situated below the first pair in rank and standing.
rows.anchor: مبتدأو ومن دون تينك الجنتين

rows.speaker: ابن زيد والأكثرون
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd and most authorities assign the first pair to the foremost and the later two to the people of the right.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد والأكثرون الأو للسابقين

rows.speaker: أبو موسى
rows.claim: Abu Musa transmits from the Prophet that the two gardens for those fearing their Lord are gold for the brought-near and silver for the people of the right.
rows.anchor: عن أبي موسى عن النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the first gardens are for the foremost and the later pair for their followers.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن : الأوليان للسابقين والأخريان للتابعين

rows.speaker: أبو موسى
rows.claim: A version of Abu Musa’s report is transmitted as a Companion statement and authenticated by al-Hakim.
rows.anchor: وروي موقوفاوصححه الحاكعن أبي موسى

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the later gardens are for descendants joined to those who fear God; al-Alusi says he found no supporting transmitted evidence.
rows.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن الأولين للخائفين والآخرين لذرياتهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Baḥr cites Ibn Abbas taking ‘below them’ as nearness for the blessed and the later-mentioned gardens as superior because their descriptions are more laudatory.
rows.anchor: وحكى في البحر عن ابن عباس أنه قال : ( ومن دونها )
